summary: SOW template to convert $2,500 audit roadmaps into $5-8k build contracts.
content:
AOM AI Operations: Build-Phase Proposal + SOW Template

Date: 2026-03-12 Agent: Alex (Deal Architect) Purpose: Convert the $2,500 audit roadmap into a $5-8k build contract. Fast, professional, no-fluff.

HOW TO USE THIS TEMPLATE

After the audit delivers a ranked roadmap of automation opportunities, the client picks their top 2-3 items. This template turns those picks into a signed contract. Fill in the bracketed fields with client-specific data from the audit.

Time to customize: 30 minutes max. The audit does the heavy lifting.

PART 1: THE PROPOSAL

AOM AI Operations Build Proposal

Prepared for: [Client Name], [Company Name] Prepared by: Patrik Matheson, AOM (Ahead of Market) Date: [Date] Valid for: 30 days from date above

1. Executive Summary

[Client Name], during your AI Operations Audit we mapped [X] hours per week of admin time across your [team size]-person team. We identified [Y] automation opportunities and scored each one on time impact and feasibility.

You selected [Z] automations to build first. Here's what that looks like.

Bottom line: [Z] automations will recover approximately [X] hours per week for your team, valued at $[amount]/month based on your $[rate]/hour effective rate. The system pays for itself in [N] months.

2. Scope of Work

Based on your audit roadmap (delivered [audit date]), the following automations will be built, tested, and deployed:

  • What it does: [One paragraph, plain English. No jargon.]

  • Estimated time savings: [X] hours/week
  • Complexity tier: [Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3]

Automation 2: [Name]

  • What it does: [Description]
  • Current process: [Current state]
  • After automation: [Future state]
  • Estimated time savings: [X] hours/week
  • Complexity tier: [Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3]

Automation 3: [Name] (if applicable)

  • What it does: [Description]
  • Current process: [Current state]
  • After automation: [Future state]
  • Estimated time savings: [X] hours/week
  • Complexity tier: [Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3]

3. Timeline

All builds follow a 4-phase process. Total timeline: 3-6 weeks depending on complexity and client responsiveness.

Phase Duration What Happens
Phase 1: Setup Week 1 Access provisioning, tool integrations, data mapping. AOM connects to your existing systems (CRM, email, scheduling, etc.). Client provides credentials and access.
Phase 2: Build Weeks 2-3 AOM builds each automation. Internal testing against your real data. Client gets progress updates every 3 business days.
Phase 3: Testing Week 4 Client team tests each automation in live environment. AOM fixes issues within 24 hours. Adjustments based on real-world usage.
Phase 4: Handoff Week 5 Training session for your team (1-2 hours, recorded). Documentation delivered. 30-day support period begins.

Note: Timeline assumes client provides access and feedback within 2 business days of each request. Delays on client side extend the timeline proportionally.

4. Pricing

Complexity Tiers

Tier Description Examples Price Range
Tier 1: Simple Single-function automations. One trigger, one action, minimal integrations. Email triage and auto-response, calendar scheduling automation, basic reporting dashboards, invoice generation $2,000 - $3,000
Tier 2: Medium Multi-step workflows. Multiple triggers, conditional logic, 2-3 tool integrations. Multi-step lead qualification pipeline, integrated scheduling + CRM + email workflows, custom client-facing dashboards with live data, automated estimating with material lookups $3,000 - $5,000
Tier 3: Complex Multi-system architectures. Custom AI pipelines, data architecture, agent-based systems. Multi-agent operations systems, custom AI pipelines with training data, full data architecture and migration, cross-platform automation with business logic $5,000 - $8,000

5. What's Included

Included in the build price:

  • All development, configuration, and integration work
  • Internal QA and testing before client handoff
  • 1 training session for your team (up to 2 hours, recorded)
  • Written documentation for each automation
  • 30-day post-launch support (bug fixes, adjustments, questions)
  • All tools and infrastructure provisioned and configured
  • Progress updates every 3 business days during the build

Not included (available as add-ons or through the retainer):

  • New automations not listed in the scope above
  • Changes to scope after project kickoff (see Change Request Process below)
  • Ongoing management, monitoring, and optimization (covered by the retainer)
  • Third-party software subscription costs (client pays directly)
  • Custom integrations with tools not discussed during the audit
  • On-site visits beyond the initial setup (remote delivery is standard)

6. Terms and Conditions

Project start: Within 5 business days of signed agreement and initial payment.

Intellectual property: All custom automations, workflows, and configurations built for [Company Name] are owned by [Company Name] upon final payment. AOM retains the right to use anonymized methods and approaches in future work.

Confidentiality: AOM will not share, publish, or disclose [Company Name]'s business data, processes, or proprietary information. NDA available upon request.

Cancellation: Client may cancel the project at any time. Work completed to date is billed at the applicable tier rate. Unused portion of the kickoff payment is refundable only if cancellation occurs before Phase 2 (Build) begins. No refund once build work has started.

Warranty: All automations are warranted to function as described in the scope for 30 days after handoff. Bugs and errors are fixed at no cost during this period. Changes to scope or new features are not covered by the warranty.

Liability: AOM's total liability is limited to the total project fee. AOM is not liable for indirect, consequential, or lost-revenue damages.

Communication: All project communication via email and scheduled check-ins. Emergency support available via phone during business hours (Monday-Friday, 9am-5pm AZ time).

7. Retainer Transition

After the 30-day support period, your automations are live and working. Here's what happens next:

Option A: Self-manage. You own everything we built. Run it yourself. We're available for one-off fixes at our hourly rate ($150/hour, billed in 30-minute increments).

Option B: AOM Managed (Recommended). Monthly retainer for ongoing management, optimization, and expansion.

Retainer Tier Monthly Fee What's Included
Essentials $1,500/month Monitoring, maintenance, bug fixes, 2 hours/month of optimization or minor enhancements, monthly performance report, priority support (4-hour response).
Growth $2,250/month Everything in Essentials + 5 hours/month of optimization or new automation work, quarterly strategy review, system health audits.
Scale $3,000/month Everything in Growth + 10 hours/month of new automation builds, dedicated account manager, same-day support, monthly ROI reporting.

Retainer starts: First day after the 30-day support period ends, or earlier if client requests.

Retainer commitment: Month-to-month. No long-term contract. 30-day written notice to cancel. We earn the renewal every month.

Why most clients choose the retainer: AI moves fast. Your business changes. New bottlenecks appear. The retainer keeps your system current, optimized, and expanding. Without it, automations slowly drift out of sync with how your team actually works.

8. Next Steps

  1. Review this proposal.
  2. Ask questions (call, email, text, whatever works).
  3. Sign below and submit the 50% kickoff payment.
  4. AOM begins Phase 1 within 5 business days.

2. 30-Day Support Period

Begins the day after Phase 4 (Handoff) is complete.

What's covered:

  • Bug fixes for any automation that doesn't meet its acceptance criteria
  • Configuration adjustments based on real-world usage
  • Questions from the client's team about how to use the system
  • Minor tweaks to improve performance (within the original scope)

What's not covered:

  • New automations or features not in the original scope
  • Changes to business processes that require rebuilding an automation
  • Third-party tool outages or API changes (AOM will advise but can't control external services)

Response times during the 30-day period:

  • Critical (automation down): 4 business hours
  • Standard (adjustment needed): 1 business day
  • Question/guidance: 2 business days

3. Change Request Process

Changes happen. Here's how we handle them without derailing the project.

What counts as a change request:

  • Adding a new automation not in the original scope
  • Significantly changing the inputs, outputs, or logic of an existing automation
  • Adding new tool integrations not discussed during the audit
  • Extending the timeline due to client-side scope changes

What doesn't count (handled within the project):

  • Minor adjustments to wording, labels, or formatting
  • Bug fixes during testing
  • Configuration tweaks based on real-world usage during Phase 3

Change request process:

  1. Client or AOM identifies the change.
  2. AOM documents the change: what it is, why it's needed, impact on timeline and cost.
  3. AOM provides a written estimate within 2 business days.
  4. Client approves or declines in writing (email is fine).
  5. If approved, change is added to the SOW as an addendum. Work begins after confirmation.

Pricing for change requests:

  • Tier 1 changes (simple additions): $1,000 - $2,000
  • Tier 2 changes (workflow modifications): $2,000 - $3,500
  • Tier 3 changes (architectural changes): $3,500 - $6,000
  • Changes are quoted individually. Bundle discount does not apply to change requests.

4. Retainer Terms (Post-Build)

If the client elects to move to a retainer after the 30-day support period:

Start date: First day after support period ends, or earlier by mutual agreement.

Billing: Monthly, invoiced on the 1st, due within 15 days.

Commitment: Month-to-month. Either party may cancel with 30 days written notice.

What the retainer includes (varies by tier, see Proposal Section 7):

  • System monitoring and uptime management
  • Bug fixes and maintenance
  • Optimization based on usage data
  • New automation hours (varies by tier)
  • Performance reporting (monthly or quarterly, varies by tier)
  • Priority support with guaranteed response times

What the retainer does not include:

  • Full rebuilds of existing automations (quoted separately)
  • New tool/platform integrations not in the original build (quoted as change requests)
  • On-site visits (available at $500/visit + travel)
  • Third-party software costs

Retainer pricing (repeated from Proposal for SOW completeness):

Tier Monthly Fee Optimization/Build Hours Support Response
Essentials $1,500/month 2 hours/month 4-hour (business hours)
Growth $2,250/month 5 hours/month 4-hour (business hours)
Scale $3,000/month 10 hours/month Same-day

Unused hours: Do not roll over. Each month is fresh. This keeps AOM responsive and prevents backlog accumulation.

Rate increases: AOM may adjust retainer pricing with 60 days written notice. Client may cancel if the new pricing doesn't work.

PART 3: PRICING LOGIC REFERENCE (INTERNAL)

This section is for AOM use only. Not included in client-facing documents.

Tier Classification Guide

Use this to quickly classify automations from the audit roadmap.

Tier 1: Simple ($2,000 - $3,000)

Build time: 1-2 days Characteristics: One trigger, one action, single tool, minimal logic.

Automation Type Typical Price Notes
Email auto-triage and routing $2,000 Rules-based, no AI needed for basic version
Calendar scheduling automation $2,000 Calendly/Cal.com + CRM sync
Basic reporting dashboard $2,500 Pull from 1-2 data sources, display metrics
Invoice generation from job completion $2,500 Template-based, triggered by status change
Appointment reminder sequences $2,000 Email/SMS, time-based triggers
Simple lead capture and notification $2,000 Form -> CRM -> notification

Tier 2: Medium ($3,000 - $5,000)

Build time: 3-5 days Characteristics: Multi-step, conditional logic, 2-3 integrations, some AI components.

Automation Type Typical Price Notes
Lead qualification pipeline $4,000 Score leads, route hot/warm/cold, auto-respond
Integrated scheduling + CRM + email $3,500 Multi-tool sync with conflict handling
Custom client dashboard with live data $4,500 Multiple data sources, role-based access
Automated estimating with lookups $5,000 Material databases, labor rates, template generation
Client onboarding workflow $3,500 Document collection, task creation, status tracking
Multi-channel customer communication $4,000 Email + SMS + portal, unified inbox

Tier 3: Complex ($5,000 - $8,000)

Build time: 5-10 days Characteristics: Multi-system, custom AI, data architecture, agent-based.

Automation Type Typical Price Notes
Multi-agent operations system $8,000 Multiple AI agents with specialized roles
Custom AI pipeline with domain training $7,000 Fine-tuned models or RAG with business data
Full data architecture and migration $6,000 Database design, ETL, historical data import
Cross-platform business automation $6,500 4+ tool integrations with complex business logic
AI-powered document processing $5,500 OCR + extraction + validation + filing
Predictive scheduling/demand system $7,500 Historical data analysis + forecasting

Bundle Discount Rules

  • 3+ automations from a single proposal: 15% off total build price
  • Bundle discount does not apply to: Change requests, retainer fees, or the audit fee
  • Maximum discount: 15% (no stacking with other offers)
  • When to offer the bundle: Always. It incentivizes clients to build more upfront, which leads to higher retainer stickiness.

Pricing Negotiation Guidelines

  • Floor price: Never go below 80% of the listed tier minimum. Below that, the margins don't work.
  • Tier 1 floor: $1,600. Tier 2 floor: $2,400. Tier 3 floor: $4,000.
  • When to negotiate: Only when the client commits to a retainer at signing. A retainer commitment justifies a small build discount because the lifetime value is higher.
  • Never discount the audit. The $2,500 is the qualification gate. Discounting it attracts tire-kickers.
  • Payment terms are not negotiable. 50/50 split protects AOM from scope creep and non-payment.

Proposal-to-Close Conversion Tips

  1. Send the proposal within 48 hours of the audit delivery meeting. Momentum dies fast.
  2. Include the audit roadmap as an appendix. The client already trusts it. The proposal just prices what they already want.
  3. Highlight the bundle discount if they're considering 2 automations. "If you add a third, you save 15% on the whole package."
  4. Lead with the ROI, not the price. "This system recovers [X] hours/week, which is worth $[Y]/month. The build costs $[Z]."
  5. Name the retainer early. Don't surprise them at the end. "Most clients move to a monthly retainer after the build. Here's how that works."
  6. Follow up at 3 days, 7 days, 14 days. After 14 days, shift to a "checking in" cadence. After 30 days, the proposal expires. Offer to refresh with updated terms if they re-engage.

Template complete. Customize per client using audit data. 30 minutes max.
